RUST-00-cargo-tooling-evidence/README.md.content:
# Cargo tooling evidence

Build a reproducible Rust baseline, explain what each tool checked, and save the
observations. Both roles contain the same working program; the learner task is
the evidence record in `observations.md`. The reference contains an example
record to compare after the observations have been made.

## Target and files

Use an ordinary account with Rust 1.97.1, Cargo, rustfmt and Clippy. The manifest
declares Rust 2024 edition. This package has no third-party dependencies. Record
the actual host and target from `rustc -Vv`; Rust edition and compiler version
are different facts. A newer toolchain is a separate compatibility observation.

Extract the whole downloaded project, then enter the selected `starter` or
`solution` directory, which contains `Cargo.toml`. Keep the supplied lockfile.
The two `diagnostics/*.rs` examples are separate from the Cargo build.

```sh
rustc -Vv
cargo -V
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --locked --offline --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline -- 'A B_c/9'
```

`cargo run` prints `packet-42` and a newline; the changed argument prints `ABc9`.
The program accepts zero or one UTF-8 label argument. Invalid UTF-8 produces no
stdout, writes `label must be valid UTF-8` to stderr and returns 64. More arguments produce no stdout,
write `usage: cargo_tooling_lab [label]` to stderr, and return 64. Empty input
prints only a newline. Only ASCII letters, ASCII digits and `-` survive, in their
original order. Dashes are retained individually. The program reads no files and
makes no network requests. Label normalization alone makes no promise about the
meaning or suitability of a label in another application.

The three unit tests cover named examples, every ASCII code point and idempotence.
Explain the distinction between these cases and all possible Unicode strings.
Separate Cargo's build progress on stderr from the program's stdout and record
each command's exit status.

## Required baseline

Complete BASELINE, PREDICT, CHECKS and LIMITS in `observations.md`. Predict the
default and changed outputs before running. Explain the manifest's package,
edition and lint entries; record the supplied lockfile state. Run each command
above. A zero exit from rustfmt checks formatting; Clippy checks its enabled lints;
tests check the stated cases; a run demonstrates only that invocation. None of
these is a dependency advisory database scan.

## First Cargo workflow audit

This activity continues the same project. Finish CLEAN and COMPARE. Record one
deliberate formatting error in `src/main.rs`, observe `cargo fmt --all --check`
refuse it, then run `cargo fmt --all` and repeat the check. Do not change the
program's behavior. Run `cargo clean`, repeat the offline tests and changed
argument run, and compare the lockfile bytes before and after. Explain which
generated files returned and why an existing executable alone would be weak
evidence for the edited source.

For the comparison with a manual build loop, consider this supplied case: a C
source was edited but its old executable was run without recompilation. State
what that run proves and what a compiler invocation plus its recorded inputs
would add. Cargo automates parts of this relationship; source identity, selected
features, toolchain, target and exact command still matter.

## Choice: transfer to another input

Keep the working code and change only the input. Predict and check `café-42`,
`---`, an empty argument and a chosen punctuation-heavy label. Explain ASCII
classification, character order, empty results and argument count. Add one named
unit test, rerun the same checks, and record its exact assertion and result.

## Challenge: classify a compiler diagnostic

Read both small diagnostic files. `let moved = label` transfers ownership of the
String; the later use of `label` has no value to borrow. The corrected example
passes a shared reference to `inspect`, so the caller retains ownership for both
calls. Predict whether each file compiles, then use a temporary output directory:

```sh
mkdir -p diagnostic-output
rustc --edition=2024 --emit=metadata diagnostics/moved-value.rs -o diagnostic-output/moved.rmeta
rustc --edition=2024 diagnostics/fixed-value.rs -o diagnostic-output/fixed
./diagnostic-output/fixed
```

The first compilation is expected to fail with E0382 and produce no executable.
The second succeeds and its executable prints `packet-42` twice on separate lines.
Record actual stderr and status rather than inventing a full diagnostic transcript.
Explain why the rejected program has no runtime trace. Finish DIAGNOSTIC with the
ownership change, the preserved output goal and the limit of the compiler result.

Compare the record with the reference only after making the predictions and
capturing the commands. A successful reference run does not fill in the learner's
observations or prove an unrelated project safe.

"""Run the Cargo lesson's exact workflows against both unmodified source roles."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import tomllib

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PACK = ROOT / "RUST-00-cargo-tooling-evidence"
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--proof", type=Path, required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
args.proof = args.proof.resolve()
assert not args.proof.exists()
OUT = args.proof.parent
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
assert os.getuid() != 0, "Use an ordinary account"


def cancel(signum, _frame):
    raise SystemExit(128 + signum)


signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, cancel)
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, cancel)


def now():
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat()


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


source = {str(path.relative_to(ROOT)): path.read_bytes()
          for path in PACK.rglob("*") if path.is_file()}
assert len(source) == 14
assert all(not (ROOT / name).is_symlink() for name in source)
for name in ("test/verify_rust_cargo_tooling.py", ".github/workflows/rust-cargo-tooling.yml"):
    source[name] = (ROOT / name).read_bytes()
for name, raw in source.items():
    target = OUT / "source" / name
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(raw)
commands = []


def run(command, cwd, label, expected=0, env=None):
    entry = dict(parentTaskId="rust-cargo-tooling", parentPid=os.getpid(), command=[os.fsdecode(part) for part in command],
                 cwd=str(cwd), startTime=now(), timeoutSeconds=120)
    child = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                             stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
    entry["pid"] = child.pid
    log = OUT / "processes.jsonl"
    with log.open("a") as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="start")) + "\n")
    stdout, stderr = b"", b""
    cleanup = "owned process exited"
    try:
        stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=120)
    except BaseException:
        if child.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=3)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate()
        cleanup = "owned process group terminated and reaped"
        raise
    finally:
        with log.open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="end", endTime=now(), exitCode=child.returncode,
                                         childProcessGroupCleanup=cleanup)) + "\n")
        (OUT / (label + ".stdout.txt")).write_bytes(stdout)
        (OUT / (label + ".stderr.txt")).write_bytes(stderr)
    commands.append(dict(label=label, exitCode=child.returncode, stdoutSha256=sha(stdout), stderrSha256=sha(stderr)))
    assert child.returncode == expected, (label, child.returncode, stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
    return stdout, stderr


versions = {}
for name, argv in [("rustc", ["rustc", "-Vv"]), ("cargo", ["cargo", "-V"]),
                   ("rustfmt", ["rustfmt", "--version"]), ("clippy", ["cargo", "clippy", "--version"])]:
    versions[name] = run(argv, ROOT, "version-" + name)[0].decode()
assert "release: 1.97.1\n" in versions["rustc"]
explicit = [("packet-42!", "packet-42"), ("A B_c/9", "ABc9"), ("", ""), ("---", "---"),
            ("café-42", "caf-42"), ("🦀", ""), ("../etc/passwd", "etcpasswd"),
            ("abcXYZ019-", "abcXYZ019-"), ("\talpha\nbeta\r", "alphabeta")]
alphabet = set("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789-")
cases = list(explicit)
ascii_input = "".join(chr(code) for code in range(1, 128))
cases.append((ascii_input, "".join(character for character in ascii_input if character in alphabet)))
state = 0xC0A62024
for index in range(32):
    chars = []
    for _ in range(index):
        state = (state * 1664525 + 1013904223) % 2**32
        chars.append(chr(1 + state % 127))
    text = "".join(chars)
    cases.append((text, "".join(character for character in text if character in alphabet)))
roles = []
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rust-cargo-tooling-") as temporary:
    work = Path(temporary)
    for role in ("starter", "solution"):
        selected = PACK / role
        directory = work / role
        shutil.copytree(selected, directory)
        env = {**os.environ, "CARGO_TARGET_DIR": str(work / (role + "-target")), "CARGO_TERM_COLOR": "never"}
        manifest = tomllib.loads((directory / "Cargo.toml").read_text())
        assert manifest["package"]["edition"] == "2024" and "dependencies" not in manifest
        lock = (directory / "Cargo.lock").read_bytes()
        assert tomllib.loads(lock.decode())["package"] == [{"name": "cargo_tooling_lab", "version": "0.1.0"}]
        run(["cargo", "fmt", "--all", "--check"], directory, role + "-format", env=env)
        run(["rustfmt", "--edition", "2024", "--check", "diagnostics/moved-value.rs", "diagnostics/fixed-value.rs"], directory, role + "-diagnostic-format", env=env)
        run(["cargo", "clippy", "--locked", "--offline", "--all-targets", "--", "-D", "warnings"], directory, role + "-clippy", env=env)
        test_output = run(["cargo", "test", "--locked", "--offline"], directory, role + "-tests", env=env)[0]
        assert b"3 passed; 0 failed" in test_output
        run(["cargo", "build", "--locked", "--offline"], directory, role + "-build", env=env)
        executable = Path(env["CARGO_TARGET_DIR"]) / "debug/cargo_tooling_lab"
        assert executable.is_file()
        program = directory / "src/main.rs"
        original = program.read_bytes()
        program.write_bytes(original.replace(b"use std::process::ExitCode;", b"use std :: process :: ExitCode;", 1))
        assert program.read_bytes() != original
        bad_format = run(["cargo", "fmt", "--all", "--check"], directory, role + "-format-refusal", expected=1, env=env)[0]
        assert bad_format
        run(["cargo", "fmt", "--all"], directory, role + "-format-repair", env=env)
        assert program.read_bytes() == original
        run(["cargo", "fmt", "--all", "--check"], directory, role + "-format-rechecked", env=env)
        run(["cargo", "clean"], directory, role + "-clean", env=env)
        assert not executable.exists()
        repeated = run(["cargo", "test", "--locked", "--offline"], directory, role + "-clean-tests", env=env)[0]
        assert b"3 passed; 0 failed" in repeated
        assert run(["cargo", "run", "--locked", "--offline"], directory, role + "-cargo-run-default", env=env)[0] == b"packet-42\n"
        assert run(["cargo", "run", "--locked", "--offline", "--", "A B_c/9"], directory, role + "-cargo-run-changed", env=env)[0] == b"ABc9\n"
        assert executable.is_file() and (directory / "Cargo.lock").read_bytes() == lock
        role_out = OUT / role
        role_out.mkdir()
        shutil.copyfile(executable, role_out / "cargo_tooling_lab")
        for index, (text, expected) in enumerate(cases):
            stdout, stderr = run([str(executable), text], directory, role + "-input-" + str(index), env=env)
            assert stdout == (expected + "\n").encode() and not stderr
        stdout, stderr = run([str(executable), "first", "second"], directory, role + "-invalid-arguments", expected=64, env=env)
        assert not stdout and stderr == b"usage: cargo_tooling_lab [label]\n"
        stdout, stderr = run([os.fsencode(executable), b"\xff"], directory, role + "-invalid-utf8", expected=64, env=env)
        assert not stdout and stderr == b"label must be valid UTF-8\n"
        failed_metadata = role_out / "moved.rmeta"
        stdout, stderr = run(["rustc", "--edition=2024", "--emit=metadata", "diagnostics/moved-value.rs", "-o", str(failed_metadata)], directory, role + "-moved-diagnostic", expected=1, env=env)
        assert not stdout and b"E0382" in stderr and not failed_metadata.exists()
        corrected = role_out / "fixed"
        run(["rustc", "--edition=2024", "diagnostics/fixed-value.rs", "-o", str(corrected)], directory, role + "-fixed-build", env=env)
        stdout, stderr = run([str(corrected)], directory, role + "-fixed-run", env=env)
        assert stdout == b"packet-42\npacket-42\n" and not stderr
        assert all((directory / name).read_bytes() == (selected / name).read_bytes()
                   for name in ("Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock", "src/main.rs", "observations.md", "diagnostics/moved-value.rs", "diagnostics/fixed-value.rs"))
        roles.append(dict(role=role, formatRefusedAndRepaired=True, clippyWarningsDenied=True, unitTests=3,
                          unitSuitePassedBeforeAndAfterClean=True, cleanRemovedExecutable=True, cases=len(cases),
                          lockfileUnchanged=True, invalidArgumentExit=64, movedValueDiagnostic="E0382",
                          correctedProgramOutput="packet-42\npacket-42\n", executableSha256=sha(executable.read_bytes()),
                          correctedExecutableSha256=sha(corrected.read_bytes()), selectedSourceUnchanged=True))
assert not work.exists()
assert all((ROOT / name).read_bytes() == raw for name, raw in source.items())
proof = dict(sourceRevision=os.environ.get("SOURCE_REVISION"), compilerVersions=versions,
             sourceFiles={name: sha(raw) for name, raw in source.items()}, roles=roles, ordinaryUser=True,
             nativeExecuted=True, commands=commands, allSourceFilesUnchanged=True,
             externalDependencyDownloadsDuringChecks=False, temporarySourceCleanup=True)
args.proof.write_text(json.dumps(proof, indent=2) + "\n")
print(json.dumps(dict(roles=len(roles), independentInputCases=sum(role["cases"] for role in roles),
                     actualCommands=len(commands), temporarySourceCleanup=True)))

.github/workflows/rust-cargo-tooling.yml.content:
name: Rust Cargo tooling

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "RUST-00-cargo-tooling-evidence/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_cargo_tooling.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-cargo-tooling.yml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "RUST-00-cargo-tooling-evidence/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_cargo_tooling.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-cargo-tooling.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: "1.97.1"
      SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install the recorded course toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.97.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - name: Verify both roles and diagnostic outcomes
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_cargo_tooling.py --proof output/rust-cargo-tooling/proof.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-cargo-tooling
          path: output/rust-cargo-tooling/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error

# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.
# It is not intended for manual editing.
version = 4

[[package]]
name = "cargo_tooling_lab"
version = "0.1.0"

# Cargo tooling reference observations

## BASELINE
Record the actual compiler and Cargo versions and host/target from the local run.
The manifest specifies edition 2024, package cargo_tooling_lab 0.1.0 and forbids
unsafe Rust in this crate. Cargo.lock version 4 lists only that package; there
are no third-party dependencies. Record actual source/lock hashes separately.

## PREDICT
Default: packet-42 followed by a newline, no program stderr, status 0. A B_c/9:
ABc9 and a newline. café-42 becomes caf-42; --- stays ---. Empty input prints
one newline. Two arguments give no stdout, the usage line on stderr and status 64.
These predictions follow the ASCII letters/digits/dash contract, not a general
claim about safe filenames or identifiers.

## CHECKS
Attach the actual format, Clippy, test and run outputs and exit statuses. The
named examples test stated cases, the ASCII test covers every code point 0–127,
and the idempotence test checks one representative mixed string. Three passed
tests do not prove every input. Cargo progress is separate from program stdout.

## CLEAN
A formatting-only error is refused by cargo fmt --all --check. cargo fmt --all
repairs formatting; repeat the refusal check and all behavioral checks. cargo
clean removes generated output; the next offline test/run rebuilds it from the
recorded source. Compare actual lockfile bytes and retain observed build output.

## COMPARE
Running an old C executable after editing its source proves behavior of that
executable only. Retain the compiler command, source hashes, flags and target,
successful build status and the resulting executable's run. Cargo manages a
build graph and selected inputs, but still requires the recorded command and
source/toolchain context to make the result reproducible.

## DIAGNOSTIC
The moved-value example is refused with E0382: ownership moves into moved and
label cannot subsequently be used. It has no runtime trace. The corrected
program borrows &label twice without moving its String and prints packet-42 on
two lines. Attach the actual compiler diagnostics and corrected run; wording and
paths can differ by compiler release.

## LIMITS
Formatting checks style, Clippy checks selected lints, tests check their cases,
and one run checks one invocation. The supplied crate has no third-party
dependencies; these commands have not refreshed an advisory database or audited
other code. For the choice activity, add a real named assertion and retain its
run rather than inferring it from this reference.
